analysis.title: Investing in Switzerland: Beyond elections (November 2026)
key_insights: UBS CIO says volatility has risen in recent weeks on geopolitical risk, persistent inflation, government debt concerns, US midterm uncertainty and questions over whether AI capex can be monetized. Robust leading indicators and a reporting season showing rising revenues and profits support a positive medium-term outlook, though correction risk stays elevated.

US midterms on 3 November: UBS puts the chance Republicans keep both chambers at 10%, a divided Congress at 40% and a Democratic sweep of both chambers at 50% (chart labels). UBS expects at least one chamber to flip but without a veto-proof majority, so gridlock rises, and it does not see this as a vote against US equities.

A flipped Congress would give Democrats more bargaining power on big tech oversight, housing, social programs and renewable energy, and raises the chance of a debt ceiling fight. UBS does not expect major changes to US trade policy because the executive branch now controls it through emergency laws.

Three election principles from UBS: do not vote with a portfolio, diversify to prepare for all outcomes, and beware of supposed no-brainers. After Biden's 2020 win green energy stocks lagged and oil producers outperformed, and defense stocks underperformed after Trump's 2016 win, because party links to sectors were already priced in.

UBS flags France as the election with the largest potential policy change given tense debt and potentially extreme party positions. Spain, France, Poland and Italy vote by end 2027 and Switzerland elects a new parliament in autumn 2027.

Swiss economy: Q2 growth was around 1.5% and the output gap closed, but exceptionally strong chemical and pharmaceutical exports likely overstate the recovery. UBS expects around 1.5% growth in 2027 and inflation slightly below 1% in both 2026 and 2027, after September CPI rose to 1%.

Three risks to the Swiss outlook: Middle East tension lifting diesel and European gas prices with low gas storage, French public finances (10-year OAT-Bund spread above 150 basis points in October), and AI doubts that could halt data center construction.

Swiss equities: rising Swiss bond yields have caused a moderate correction from the mid-August all-time high. On a yield-based regression the fair SMI forward P/E is just under 17x, and the SMI trades exactly at that level on consensus 12-month earnings. UBS forecasts SMI earnings growth of 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027.

UBS tactically prefers Swiss mid-caps and quality cyclicals, with longer-term themes in Swiss high-quality dividends, defensives with growing cash flow, ROIC above 15%, and beneficiaries of AI, longevity and energy and resources. US midterm pricing pressure in health care could limit near-term upside for pharmaceutical stocks, though rhetoric may exceed actual pressure.

Global equities stay Attractive. UBS sees upside in the S&P 500 through mid-2027, expects 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, and expects Asia and emerging markets to deliver among the strongest earnings growth globally. Watchpoints for AI are enterprise productivity returns, private capital access, power availability, data center permitting and hyperscaler cash flows.

UBS says the Fed and ECB raised policy rates last month and inflation above the Fed's target points to some further US tightening. UBS does not expect higher rates to materially hurt corporate profits or slow activity.

SNB held at 0% in September. UBS base case is a first hike in March 2027 and a second to 0.5% in June 2027, largely priced in, so upside risk for longer Swiss yields is limited. In CHF bonds UBS prefers intermediate maturities and investment grade quality, with SBI AA to BBB yields of about 1.3% to 1.5% and SBI total return slightly negative year to date.

Currencies: UBS expects the euro and dollar to hold up against the franc short term (ECB hike expected in December) but sees asymmetric risks favoring the franc over 12 months as the SNB starts hiking while the ECB and Fed finish. It favors active currency hedging.

Swiss real estate: fundamentals are robust but rising rates, high valuations and rental regulation risk limit upside, so UBS keeps a neutral stance on stocks and funds. From early September to 26 October funds fell 1.2% and stocks were roughly flat.

Portfolio messages for Swiss investors: stay invested and diversify internationally because tech is under 1% of the Swiss benchmark, hold broad commodity exposure including energy, put excess cash to work, broaden AI exposure beyond a few leaders, and add alternatives while checking liquidity, leverage and fees.

sector_views.rationale: UBS expects stronger earnings momentum than the SMI this year and next.
Broadening earnings and a manufacturing PMI above 50 for seven months favor cyclical segments.
US pricing pressure in health care after the midterms is a near-term headwind to upside, though rhetoric may exceed actual pressure.
Robust rents and fundamentals are offset by rising rates, high valuations and rental regulation risk.
Tight physical markets and renewed energy supply disruption support a commodity upcycle and diversification.
AI investment drives earnings, with exposure to be spread across semiconductors, cloud, software, power and utilities. Swiss tech is under 1% of the benchmark, so UBS looks abroad.
Short-term returns are limited. UBS prefers intermediate maturities and investment grade quality.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts SMI earnings growth of 11% in 2026 and 8% in 2027 (UBS forecast).
UBS forecasts Eurozone earnings growth of 15% in both 2026 and 2027 (UBS forecast).

Consensus (FactSet, 21 Oct 2026): SMI EPS growth 9.1% in 2025 base and 10.6% in 2026F, S&P 500 34.4% in 2026F? not stated as such, see table: S&P 500 EPS growth 34.4% (2025 column), 15.6% (2026F), 7.2% (2027F column labeled differently), Euro STOXX 19.2% / 11.5%. Column mapping is ambiguous in the extracted table, so treat as consensus estimates.

Early Swiss Q3 2026 reports show strong growth in Eastern Europe, Asia and Mexico, and in semiconductor suppliers, data center construction, beauty products and pharmaceutical contract manufacturing (UBS reading of published results).

UBS SLI results scorecard for 3Q26 as of 21 Oct: 4 companies reported, 3 above consensus (75%) and 1 in line (25%), none below. Prior quarter 2Q26 was 57% above, 36% in line, 7% below across 28 companies. Upcoming dates include Nestlé, Roche, Schindler on 22 Oct, Novartis 27 Oct, Sandoz and Straumann 28 Oct, Geberit 3 Nov, Swiss Re and Swisscom 5 Nov, Zurich 12 Nov, Richemont 13 Nov.
UBS expects US Q3 earnings to remain strong, with AI-related spending the largest source of earnings growth (UBS expectation).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Output gap closed, though pharma and chemical exports likely overstate the recovery.
Low end of UBS potential growth estimate, a return to trend.
Higher than expected, supported by energy prices.

SNB held, raised inflation forecasts slightly and noted accelerating activity.
Largely priced in, so limited upside risk for long Swiss yields.

Market concern about French debt. A further sharp rise is not UBS base case.
Would widen the euro rate advantage over Switzerland and support EURCHF.
Contributes to higher global bond yields. UBS sees some further US tightening.

trade_ideas.description: Hold broad commodity exposure including energy as protection against prolonged supply disruption and inflation
trade_ideas.rationale: Renewed energy supply disruption and tight physical markets support a commodity upcycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Allocations should be actively managed and sized for volatility.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Swiss mid-caps and quality cyclicals within Swiss equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Stronger earnings momentum than the SMI this year and next.

trade_ideas.description: Buy intermediate-maturity, investment grade CHF bonds and selectively add credit risk at the short end
trade_ideas.rationale: Still-tight spreads leave little room for disappointment, and SNB hikes are priced in.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated yield volatility from global growth and elections.

trade_ideas.description: Actively hedge foreign currency exposure back to CHF
trade_ideas.rationale: Asymmetric risks favor the franc over 12 months as rate differentials narrow.
trade_ideas.risk: Euro and dollar may stay supported short term, with an ECB hike expected in December.

trade_ideas.description: Diversify AI exposure beyond a few leaders across semiconductors, cloud, software, power infrastructure, utilities and industrials
trade_ideas.rationale: AI investment remains a major driver of earnings and activity.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated valuations, execution risk and wide differences in company outcomes.

risk_factors: Geopolitical energy disruption and a cold winter with low gas storage.
French sovereign stress spilling into European growth and the euro.
AI monetization doubts leading to halted data center construction and weaker global investment.
Persistent inflation prompting more restrictive central banks and higher bond yields that weigh on P/E ratios.
US debt ceiling conflict and regulatory uncertainty after the midterms.
Swiss rental regulation (rental price initiative) and high real estate valuations.
Possible polling errors in elections, as with the 2016 Brexit referendum.
charts_described: UBS chart: probabilities for the US midterms of 50% Democrats win both chambers, 40% divided Congress and 10% status quo, as of 21 October 2026.
Chart of French and German 10-year yields and their spread, with the spread above 150 basis points in October 2026.
Chart of SNB policy rate at 0% alongside 2-year and 10-year Swiss government bond yields, as of 20 October 2026.
vol_and_positioning: Market volatility has risen significantly in recent weeks, and the risk of market corrections is likely to remain elevated.
UBS suggests using market strength to reduce concentrated single-stock positions and checking that single asset classes or stocks are not too dominant.
Rapidly shifting sentiment around AI risks is an additional source of volatility. Higher rates and financing stress are greater risks for new compute suppliers than for hyperscalers.
Active currency hedging is becoming more attractive for CHF-based investors.
geopolitical: Middle East tensions have lifted diesel and European natural gas prices, with low gas storage a winter risk for Europe.
US midterm elections on 3 November, with Democrats favored to take at least one chamber and a potential debt ceiling fight.
French public finances and the widening OAT-Bund spread ahead of French elections.
Series of elections ahead in Spain, France, Poland and Italy by end 2027, and a Swiss parliamentary vote in autumn 2027.
US trade policy kept with the executive branch via emergency laws, so little change expected from the midterms.
Potential trade restrictions flagged on Samsung, TSMC and HDFC Bank in the Global Top List.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors in US equities are buying the innovation of US companies. The S&P 500 gained around 80% in USD over five years, and trade policy is unlikely to change.
tension_points.bear_case: A Democratic win raises gridlock, big tech oversight demands and debt ceiling conflict, which could fuel market anxiety.

tension_points.bull_case: Short term the euro and dollar are supported by higher rates, and the euro should regain ground as French fiscal worries ease and the ECB hikes in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Over 12 months the SNB starts hiking while the ECB and Fed finish, and persistent inflation would raise growth concerns that benefit the franc as a defensive asset.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If inflation falls faster than expected, rate hike expectations abroad fall and support the franc, while a further inflation rise first widens the differential in favor of euro and dollar.

tension_points.bull_case: AI-related spending is the largest source of US Q3 earnings growth, and hyperscaler balance sheets provide a buffer.
tension_points.bear_case: Doubts about monetization could halt data center construction, and private capital access, power availability and permitting are bottlenecks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of weak enterprise productivity returns or loss of private capital funding for AI demand.

theme_stances.key_argument: Midterms look like a vote against the administration but not against US equities, and diversification is the best preparation.
theme_stances.evidence: we do not view this as a vote against US equities in general

theme_stances.key_argument: High rate expectations abroad will be hard to meet and persistent inflation could trigger growth concerns that lift the franc.
theme_stances.evidence: Over a 12-month horizon, asymmetric risks favor the Swiss franc.

theme_stances.key_argument: Broadening earnings momentum and an industrial recovery favor mid-caps and quality cyclicals over the SMI.
theme_stances.evidence: Tactically, we prefer Swiss mid-caps and quality cyclicals.
